required_coverage.detail: Table 5 uses breadth at t−1, t, and t+1. The paper says CDA/Spectrum data cover 1982–2004, so actual report-date endpoints and the extra conservative years must be checked.

implementation_issues.description: The general Section 3 definition and Table 5 note give opposite signs for size-adjusted returns. The assessment follows the general firm-minus-size-portfolio definition (p. 7), which is also consistent with the p. 24 negative breadth-return interpretation, and flags the table-specific reversal. The paper does not explicitly reconcile the two statements, so the original Table 5 coding cannot be confirmed from the frozen source alone.

Breadth scale conflicts: Table 5 says multiply by 100, while the main fraction definition and the p. 24 interpretation of 0.01 as one percentage point support an unscaled proportion. The construction uses the unscaled fraction and retains the table-note conflict for review.

The daily excess-return subtraction order is reversed between Section 3 and the Table 5 note. The construction follows Section 3; because the difference is squared, reversing the sign does not change the daily squared-excess-return input.

evidence.quote: To ensure that our measure captures changes in the breadth of ownership rather than changes in the universe of institutions covered by our database, we compute this variable using only 13F filers that exist in our database in both quarters t and t - 1.
evidence.description: The main text defines a change in the proportion of filers, with the t−1 filer universe as the denominator, and restricts the change to filers present in both adjacent quarters.

evidence.quote: Data on the 13F filers is obtained from the CDA/Spectrum 13F institutional transaction quarterly data, covering the period from 1982 through 2004.
evidence.description: The paper names CDA/Spectrum and states quarterly holdings coverage from 1982 through 2004.

evidence.quote: Stock return data are extracted from the CRSP monthly and daily return files,
evidence.description: The frozen baseline needs CRSP monthly returns for future outcomes and daily returns for the risk calculation.

evidence.quote: We use size-adjusted returns, computed as the difference between the security’s return and the return on the security’s size-matched decile portfolio over the corresponding period.
evidence.description: Section 3 gives the firm-minus-size-portfolio sign for the dependent variable.

evidence.quote: Sizematched portfolios are based on decile assignments of market capitalization for all NYSE/AMEX stocks.
evidence.description: The size benchmark uses a distinct NYSE/AMEX population, separate from the final estimation sample.

evidence.quote: We measure quarterly (annual) idiosyncratic risk as the square root of the sum over the prior 3 (12) months of monthly idiosyncratic risk measures.
evidence.description: The source supports 3-month and 12-month risk windows.

evidence.quote: the monthly measures equal the sum of daily squared excess returns. Excess returns are computed by subtracting the daily value-weighted industry return from the security’s daily return.
evidence.description: The source requires daily stock returns and a daily value-weighted industry return series.

evidence.quote: Industry classifications are based on Fama and French (1997).
evidence.description: The source identifies the Fama–French industry classification used for daily excess returns.

evidence.quote: our idiosyncratic risk measures are ranked into deciles and the ranks are normalized to range from -0.5 to 0.5.
evidence.description: The source specifies a decile rank normalized to −0.5 through +0.5 but does not define the rank universe.

evidence.quote: Our sample period is restricted to the 23-year period from 1982 to 2004 due to lack of institutional ownership data prior to 1982.
evidence.description: The paper states its institutional ownership period cutoff; it does not establish local snapshot coverage or the report-date basis of that cutoff.

evidence.quote: We compute both quarterly changes and annual changes once every quarter, resulting in overlapping annual return measurement intervals.
evidence.description: Annual breadth and return measurements roll every quarter rather than using non-overlapping calendar-year bins.

evidence.quote: Panel A (B) of this table reports mean coefficient estimates and t-statistics from quarterly regressions of one-quarter-ahead (1-year-ahead) size-adjusted returns on prior, current, and next period measures of the change investor recognition and their interactive terms with idiosyncratic risk.
evidence.description: Table 5 identifies the frozen baseline horizons and the prior/current/next predictor periods.

evidence.quote: The requirement of variable leads and lags reduced the sample size to 90 quarters in Panel A (1982Q2–2004Q3) and 84 quarters in Panel B (1983Q1–2003Q4).
evidence.description: The final baseline is a repeated quarterly cross-section with reported quarter ranges; the item records average N, not exact quarter-specific Ns.

evidence.quote: Size-adjusted returns are computed as the difference between the return on a firm’s size decile portfolio return and the return for the firm during quartert+k or yeart+k.
evidence.description: Table 5 reverses the return subtraction order stated in Section 3.

evidence.quote: Percentage quarterly change in breadth (DBreadthQTR) equals the difference in the number of institutions (13F filers) holding the firm’s stock at the beginning and at the end of the quarter divided by the total number of institutions at the beginning of the quarter and multiplied by 100.
evidence.description: The Table 5 note says to multiply quarterly breadth changes by 100.

evidence.quote: Percentage annual change in breadth (DBreadthANN) equals the difference in the number of institutions holding the firm’s stock at the end of quarter t - 4 and at the end of the current quarter divided by the total number of institutions at the end of quarter t - 4, and multiplied by 100.
evidence.description: Annual breadth compares current-quarter holdings with quarter t−4 holdings and uses the earlier-quarter filer count as denominator.

evidence.quote: The monthly measures equal the sum of the daily squared excess return, which equal the difference between the daily value-weighted industry return and the firm’s daily returns.
evidence.description: The Table 5 note reverses the daily excess-return subtraction order; the difference is squared before aggregation.

evidence.quote: The idiosyncratic risk measures are ranked each quarter into deciles and the ranks are normalized to range from -.5 to +.5 (denoted Rank i-risk).
evidence.description: Table 5 confirms quarterly ranking but leaves the ranking population unstated.

evidence.quote: The t-statistics are adjusted using the Newey–West correction with four lags
evidence.description: Standard errors for the time-series mean coefficients use four quarterly Newey–West lags.

evidence.quote: an increase in DBREADTH of 0.01 (i.e., attracting an additional 1% of existing institutional investors)
evidence.description: The economic interpretation supports an unscaled fraction rather than the Table 5 percentage-times-100 note.

evidence.quote: For brevity, we omit main effects for Rank irisk in periods t - 1 and t + 1, because Rank i-risk is very highly autocorrelated.
evidence.description: The frozen final specification has only the period-t standalone risk effect; do not add risk main effects at t−1 or t+1.
